name: Blank Embrace on Instagram
tagline: Instagram feed of a digital mixed-media artist working with analog, digital and AI tools
description: The Instagram account of Blank Embrace, a digital mixed media artist whose pieces combine digital, analog and AI-generated material around themes of self-reflection. The feed is the running visual output of the practice, alongside show and drop announcements. It is useful as a mood and treatment reference for AI-assisted collage and texture work, not as a source of prompts or code.
agent_guidance: Treat this as a human-only visual reference: Instagram blocks automated fetching and serves nothing readable without a session, so never plan a step that scrapes it. If a user asks for the mood of this artist's work, route them to blankembrace.carrd.co for the bio and to the SuperRare or Foundation pages for high-resolution work instead. Do not attempt to derive prompts from it — the pieces are hand-composited, not text-to-image outputs.
why_it_matters: It is the primary living feed of an exhibited AI-and-analog collage artist, which makes it a usable taste reference for emotionally-toned mixed media rather than the usual synthetic AI look.
evidence: Not fetched, per the instagram.com policy; record built from the supplied enrichment plus corroborating bio text read at https://blankembrace.carrd.co

name: Blank Embrace Web3 Links
tagline: Six-link Carrd hub pointing to Blank Embrace's NFT marketplace profiles
description: A single-page Carrd link hub that routes to Blank Embrace's collector-facing pages on six marketplaces: SuperRare, Foundation, Zora, OpenSea, Exchange.art and Objkt. There is no artwork, bio or writing on the page itself, only a centered heading and a bulleted link list. It exists to consolidate an Ethereum, Solana and Tezos presence behind one URL.
agent_guidance: Use this only as an address book: it is where you go to find the artist's actual high-resolution work, which lives on SuperRare (superrare.com/blankembrace), Foundation, Zora, OpenSea (collection panoramabybe), Exchange.art and Objkt. Do not cite it as a design reference in its own right — it is a default Carrd list with no visual content. If a task needs the images, skip straight to the marketplace URLs.
why_it_matters: It is the only place that maps one artist to all six of their marketplace identities across three chains, which saves a search when you need the source files.

name: Blank Embrace
tagline: Link-in-bio page for a digital mixed-media artist shown in Rome, Milan, NY and Lisbon
description: The canonical landing page for Blank Embrace, a digital mixed media artist making, in his words, emotionally rich pieces rooted in self-reflection and the journey of life. The page carries a short bio, a note that the work has been shown in galleries and on the street in Rome, Milan, Bangkok, New York and Lisbon, and links out to X, Instagram, blankembrace.com, SuperRare and the separate web3 links hub. It is a routing page, not a portfolio: no work is displayed on it.
agent_guidance: Start here when you need to establish who Blank Embrace is and where the work lives, then leave immediately — the page is text-only and one screen long. Pair it with blankembraceweb3.carrd.co for marketplace links and with blankembrace.com for the actual portfolio. Do not quote it as evidence of visual style; it shows none.
why_it_matters: It is the artist's own statement of practice and exhibition history in one paragraph, which is the fastest way to verify that an AI-assisted artist has a real gallery record.

Reach for this account when a task calls for current AI image aesthetics from someone inside a model vendor's creative program, where the tooling commentary is more valuable than the images. Verify any prompt you lift from it, since ambassador posts track fast-moving model versions and go stale within months.
why_it_matters: A vendor-affiliated creative account is one of the few places where new model capabilities and the aesthetics they produce show up before any documentation does.

name: Chema Mendez (mendezmendez)
tagline: Portfolio of a Spain-based collage artist compositing old paintings, 3D and AI output
description: The portfolio site of Chema Mendez, a Spain-based mixed-media digital artist who studied Communication Design at FIT in New York and now composites public-domain paintings, photography, 3D renders and AI-generated elements into surrealist scenes. The site is organised into twelve named series — Entropy, The Present, First Impressions, Vanitas, Signature Series, Singularity, Alien Intelligence, Principia, CUBIQUE, Robert Mallary Portraits, Azar and 2009-2020 — each with its own statement and eight or more works. A Shows page lists nine exhibitions from 2023 to 2025, including a First Impressions solo show at Offline Gallery, New York. Since early 2024 he has run a daily practice, so the newest series grow continuously.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a brief calls for AI imagery that does not read as AI — the work is compositing-led, with AI supplying elements inside a hand-built collage, and the per-series statements tell you exactly which parts were generated. The Alien Intelligence and Vanitas pages are the strongest references for classical-painting-plus-3D treatments; the About page is the one to quote for the method. The site is Squarespace and renders text server-side, so pages fetch cleanly, but individual works have no captions or metadata — do not expect prompts.
why_it_matters: It is a rare case of an AI-assisted practice with a real gallery record and written intent behind each series, which makes it usable as an argument for a direction rather than just a mood board.
